title: Japan’s Nuclear Taboo Is Starting to Crack
author: Jio Kamata
text:
Credit: Depositphotos
August has been a solemn month in Japan for more than 80 years. Although Japan formally signed the Instrument of Surrender on September 2, 1945, the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on August 6 and 9, respectively, and Emperor Hirohito’s radio announcement on August 15 accepting the terms of surrender have made August a month from which the Japanese psyche cannot escape. Every year since the Pacific War ended in Japan’s defeat, during August the nation has mourned its war dead and reflected on the horrors of a conflict that inflicted immense suffering and destruction upon the country. The resolve that Japan must never again endure such an ordeal lingers in the air of the sweltering Japanese summer.But this year, another issue besides the memory of war has been generating heated debate in the Japanese media: will the Takaichi administration revise the government’s Three Non-Nuclear Principles in the upcoming revision of Japan’s national security documents? [...]
